newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania Jan state budget deficit 337.7 bln lei.
newsitem.headline: Romania Jan state budget deficit 337.7 bln lei.

text.p: Romania's state budget posted a deficit of 337.7 billion lei in January, compared with 207.2 billion lei in January 1996, central bank (BNR) data showed on Monday.
State revenues amounted to 2.13 trillion lei in January, when spending was 2.46 trillion, BNR data showed.
The new centrist coalition government, which ousted leftists in last year's elections, approved the 1997 draft budget, a plank under loan accords with international lenders, on Saturday.
Under the draft, the 1997 state budget deficit was set at 12.6 trillion lei or 5.4 percent of the gross domestic product. The BNR data put the 1996 state budget gap at 5.6 trillion lei.

The 1997 bill also forecast a consolidated budget deficit lower at 4.5 percent of the GDP, against 5.8 percent in 1996. The consolidated budget includes state budget, local government budgets, social security budget, supplementary pension funds and various other extra-budgetary funds.
The BNR data showed local budgets had a 82.6 billion lei surplus in January, when the social security budget had a 31.2 billion lei gap.
Parliament, where the ruling coalition has a comfortable majority, is expected to endorse the draft within one month.

The budget gap was agreed with the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank last month. Both institutions suspended loans for Romania over foreign exchange curbs and overspending by the former ruling leftists in the 1996 election year.
Romania hopes to get around $1.0 billion in combined loans from the Fund and World Bank to underpin tough market reforms.
The 1997 budget gap would be financed through external credits -- about 3.4 percent -- with the rest funded by domestic loans.
